title: Finite approximation retaining an idempotent congruence
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings with B a finite type A-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], I an ideal of A, and S the integral closure of A in B [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Suppose g in S has idempotent image in S/IS and the canonical localization map S[1/g] to B[1/g] is bijective [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. There exist an A-subalgebra D of B finite as an A-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and b in D with b=g in B, idempotent image in D/ID, and bijective canonical localization map D[1/b] to B[1/b].

source.place: Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), proof of (5) implies (2), construction and closed-fibre decomposition of B''; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09XI, read 2026-10-12

proof.text: Choose finite algebra generators x of B. Localization surjectivity, using Localization.awayMap_surjective_iff, supplies y(x) in S and m(x) with y(x)=g^m(x)*x. The idempotent congruence says g*g-g belongs to IS.

Apply Mathlib Finsupp.mem_span_range_iff_exists_finsupp to the extended-ideal membership of g*g-g. Obtain finitely supported coefficients l indexed by elements of I. Let t contain g, the finitely many y(x), and l(a) for every a in l.support, and put T=Algebra.adjoin A t. Every l(a) belongs to T: it is a listed generator on the support and zero off the support. The finite sum of these coefficients times algebraMap A T a equals g*g-g in T by injectivity of its inclusion, so this element belongs to IT. No separate finite-subalgebra membership or congruence theorem is used.

Every element of the integral closure S is integral over A. Apply Mathlib Algebra.finite_adjoin_of_finite_of_isIntegral directly to the finite set t to make T module-finite. Map T along the injective inclusion S to B, obtaining D and an algebra equivalence T to D. Transport finiteness and the ideal witness, and put b equal to the image of g.

Localization preserves the injective inclusion D to B. The localized image contains every x=y(x)/b^m(x), hence the algebra generated by all x. It also contains b inverse. Write any fraction as a numerator times a power of b inverse to obtain surjectivity. These calculations are implemented using IsLocalization.map_injective_of_injective, localization fraction normal forms, and the generating-set equality.

theorem exists_finite_integral_away_approximation
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Algebra.FiniteType A B] (I : Ideal A) (g : integralClosure A B)
    (hg : IsIdempotentElem
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A (integralClosure A B))) g))
    (hloc : Function.Bijective
      (Localization.awayMap (integralClosure A B).val.toRingHom g)) :
    ∃ (D : Subalgebra A B) (_ : Module.Finite A D) (b : D),
      b.1 = g.1 ∧ IsIdempotentElem (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A D)) b) ∧
      Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap D.val.toRingHom b)
